source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building accessibility checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Document the date and time of the inspection.
3. Note the specific location and building ID (if applicable).
4. List the exact accessibility requirements or regulations not being met.
   - Use codes/standards such as ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act), ANSI, or local building codes.
   - Specify the exact sections or guidelines of the standards that are not being followed.
5. Describe the accessibility issues in detail.
   - Indicate what specific accessibility features are missing or non-compliant.
   - Provide precise measurements or technical observations.
   - Document with photos (if allowed) to support your findings.
6. Note any safety hazards related to the non-compliance.
   - Include details on how these hazards could affect users with disabilities.
7. Document the overall condition of the building if it impacts accessibility.
   - Mention any wear, damage, or obstructions that hinder accessibility.
8. Indicate whether remedial work had previously been recommended and if
